prompt:
A native embedded device screen in portrait 3:4 (240x320 TFT), shown flat and edge to edge with crisp readable text, no device body, hands or desk around it. It is the startup screen of BayuPandu, an open-source paragliding variometer ("bayu" = wind, "pandu" = guide), shown for about three seconds when the pilot switches the instrument on at launch, while it checks its sensors. The reference image is a real BayuPandu screen: carry over its green highway-sign panel with white border and rounded corners on a near-black surround, white heavy Overpass road-sign lettering in capitals, and flat polygon sign symbols; do not copy its flight numbers or layout. No yellow anywhere: yellow is reserved for warnings.

The BayuPandu mark is a flat white sign symbol: a paraglider wing seen from the front, a wide shallow arc divided into cells, carried on three short horizontal wind lines beneath it. No pilot figure, no lines to a harness, no gradients: it must read like a pictogram on a road sign.

What leads: wind. Many white horizontal streaks of different lengths cross the whole sign from left to right, like wind on a weather chart; toward the centre they converge and become the three wind lines under the wing, so the mark forms out of the wind itself. Under the mark, the wordmark BAYUPANDU and V0.1.0 small. At the bottom, one compact line of the startup checks: BARO OK  GPS OK  LOG OK  BATT 92%. A small caption at the very bottom: ANY BUTTON TO SKIP.
